No Result View All Result Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us Hausa Edition Home News Politics Business Sport Football Health Entertainment Education Opinion Editorial Columns Others LeVogue Magazine Conferences National Economy Contact Us No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Terrorism: Group Urges FG To Partner Developed Countries by Nonye Ekwenugo 3 seconds ago in Religion Share on WhatsApp Share on Facebook Share on X Telegram A group, Christian United for Israel Prayer Outreach, North-West zone, has urged the federal government to partner with developed countries to strengthen Nigeria’s capacity to tackle terrorism and other security challenges.
The group’s North-West Coordinator, Dr John Ikpeme, made the call at its end-of-year dinner in Kaduna, saying the government and security agencies were overstretched by persistent terrorist attacks across the country. He said the attacks had resulted in the loss of innocent lives, destruction of property and displacement of communities, forcing many residents to abandon their ancestral homes in search of safety.
Ikpeme said Nigeria needed international cooperation, particularly in the area of technical expertise, to effectively confront terrorist groups and other criminal elements.
He argued that the country lacked the technical know-how required to adequately address the security challenges, adding that collaboration with developed nations would help strengthen efforts to restore peace.
According to him, sustained insecurity has also hindered national development and subjected citizens to hardship, making it necessary for all stakeholders to work towards finding lasting solutions.
He said Nigeria was endowed with abundant human and natural resources, stressing that a peaceful environment was necessary for citizens to maximise their potential and improve their living standards.
Ikpeme added that the group continued to pray for peace in Nigeria, Israel and other parts of the world, expressing hope for divine intervention to restore peace and unity.
He said peace was essential for people to carry out their normal economic and social activities and improve their livelihoods.
